dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"All 41 controls in the log match annual recharge rows by dealer/posting date, count, total, and effective-date range."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 17 records total $1,506.29 and reconcile exactly to the two dealer controls."
"The flagged rows were posted 3–30 days after their effective dates (mean 15.65 days), and none was posted before its effective date."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "A duplicate general-ledger entry remains outside the supplied evidence."
"Intent cannot be conclusively assessed without contracts and audit history."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Open a read-only reconciliation ticket for the 17 source event IDs: attach the raw dealer files and contract clauses, trace cash, entitlement, and general-ledger entries, and produce a shadow weekly trend using `effective_event_date`."
"Keep production records unchanged and retain the existing posted-date view until the trace is signed off."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Do not escalate the 31 May cluster as duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a pipeline defect."
"The weekly trend pack may be distorted if it groups activity by `posted_at`, but the underlying effective dates are preserved."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "There is no duplicate key signal" is appropriately supported for the tested recharge and source-event keys, but it should not be read as ruling out every possible form of duplicate revenue, particularly duplicate general-ledger postings or entitlement delivery.

"Pipeline defect: rejected as the primary explanation" is reasonable for the observed controls, but matching controls do not by themselves exclude a defect that altered posting dates or affected an untested downstream process. The submission partly addresses this by limiting the judgment and recommending a shadow trend.

The statement that operations says contracts permit monthly files is cited to the email, but contractual permission is not independently verified; the submission explicitly acknowledges this limitation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A residual alternative is an unauthorized or downstream duplication/processing issue not visible in the recharge and dealer-control files—for example, duplicate cash settlement, entitlement delivery, general-ledger booking, or altered source dates. The analyst handled this well by preserving those as unknowns and specifying the evidence that would change the decision, while also considering pipeline defect and manipulated reporting.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Execute and document the proposed joins to cash, entitlement, and general-ledger records, and independently verify the dealer contracts and raw submissions; this would convert the current strong recharge/import conclusion into a complete duplicate-revenue and entitlement conclusion.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South cases fell 318 to 196 (6.12 to 3.77/day; -38%), while non-South cases rose 707 to 746 (+6%); the unadjusted controlled before/after ratio implies a 42% relative reduction."
"Post-launch South had 2,709 IVR sessions: 507 errors (18.7%), 591 abandonments (21.8%), 650 endings at `authenticate` (24.0%), and only 94 case IDs (3.5%)."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The evidence supports a reduction in recorded CareDesk cases in South, not a causal improvement in customer experience."
"Nova coincided with a changed funnel or capture process: South IVR records rose 197 to 2,709, and many journeys failed or ended before a case could be created."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "With no verified task completion, satisfaction, eligible-caller denominator, or randomized control, causality and customer benefit remain unproven."
"The non-South comparison contradicts a company-wide seasonal decline as the sole explanation, and the service-event data contradict fewer recorded South disruptions as the sole explanation."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet."
"Keep only a tightly monitored South validation with an automatic agent fallback for authentication/error loops."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "decide on verified task completion, same-issue 7-day repeat contact, error/abandonment, cases per eligible caller, CSAT and harm/escalation rates—not containment alone."

"Can you provide a subscriber-linked 1-, 7-, and 14-day repeat-contact cut by terminal stage and outcome across IVR, agent, app, and dealer channels, with sampled reasons showing whether repeats were for the same issue?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "many journeys failed or ended before a case could be created" is directionally plausible from the IVR records and low case-ID rate, but the supplied evidence does not by itself establish that every error or abandonment represented a would-be complaint or that the journey would otherwise have generated a case.

"Run for at least two complete weeks" may be operationally short for stable 7- and 14-day repeat-contact outcomes unless the stated pre-specified sample-size threshold and follow-up window extend beyond the two-week run.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled seasonality, fewer service disruptions, duplicate/orphan records, and the possibility that repeat contacts concerned different issues. The strongest remaining alternative is that South IVR volume and case-count changes reflect routing, eligibility, promotion, logging, or population-mix changes rather than a pure capture failure or customer-experience change; the submission preserves this uncertainty and explicitly requests denominator and change-record reconciliation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the capture-failure mechanism directly testable by linking eligible inbound calls through every IVR stage to case creation, agent fallback, task completion, and same-issue repeat contact, supplemented by sampled recordings/transcripts; explicitly distinguish abandonment as an observation from complaint or dissatisfaction as an outcome.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies `inverter_events.csv`, all four rows, and specific fields (`severity`, `duration_min`, `impact_mw`) for the warning count, durations, clearance, and zero impact.
It appropriately limits the validation claim to the export: “High for the export; not proof beyond its scope.”
The claim that `INV-17` has no repeat in the export is explicitly scoped to that file.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission distinguishes an event-name pattern from a demonstrated failure and rejects the thermal/DC-fault hypothesis using different inverters, different dates, informational severity, clearance, and zero impact.
It considers the innocent explanation that a communication gap may merely affect telemetry and does not treat `COMM_LINK_WARN` as proof of a plant fault.
The analysis remains primarily within one event export and does not yet triangulate an independent heartbeat, telemetry, or SCADA channel; it correctly proposes that as the next check.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It labels the communication-warning follow-up confidence as “moderate” and the thermal/DC-fault rejection as “high,” rather than using one blanket confidence level.
It explicitly states that event wording alone cannot establish a communication problem and that the export does not prove conditions beyond its scope.
The stopping rule is conditional: escalate only for an unexplained data gap or recurrence.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—“Perform one cheap check, then stop unless it fails”—is proportionate to seven minutes of warning duration, zero recorded MW impact, clearance, and no repeat in the export.
The proposed check of the `INV-17` communication heartbeat or telemetry-availability log for approximately 09:35–09:55 on 2026-05-27 is targeted and decision-changing.
It preserves an operational escalation path without inventing a plant fault or searching indefinitely for a story.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately treats the isolated seven-minute communication warning as a low-cost verification item rather than an escalation-worthy inverter failure.
It incorporates the key visible facts cited in the submission: sole warning, cleared event, zero MW impact, and no recurrence in the four-row export.
It also appropriately allows a mixed event-wording issue to remain only a low-priority quality check rather than a causal finding.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the file has “no blank fields, duplicate rows, or duplicate timestamps” is asserted as a full-file validation result, but the submission does not show the validation method or the actual timestamps; it is appropriately limited to the export, so this is a minor evidence-detail gap rather than a material overstatement.
The proposed 09:35–09:55 window is not justified in the submission by quoting the exact event timestamp or timezone conversion; it should be tied explicitly to the event row.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: `COMM_LINK_WARN` could represent a transient communications or logging artifact with no equipment consequence; alternatively, it could indicate a short telemetry blind spot not captured by the event export. The proposed heartbeat/telemetry cross-check discriminates between those possibilities without assuming either one.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote the exact `INV-17` event timestamp and cross-check that same interval against an independent heartbeat, SCADA, or telemetry-availability log, explicitly recording whether there was a data gap and whether any MW/setpoint/availability signal changed.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Across the 96 15-minute blocks on each date, the data sum to Rs 662,444.09 on 28 May ... and Rs 453,085.88 on 29 May"; cites `dispatch_blocks.csv` and `AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md`.

"Applying the recorded block rates and the extract's bands to the displayed block values gives approximately Rs 549.6k under the base schedule versus the recorded Rs 453.1k"; cites `dispatch_blocks.csv` and `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf`.
The submission explicitly distinguishes descriptive totals, the conditional same-day calculation, and unsupported billed savings or net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: "This conditional, same-day calculation avoids attributing all cross-day variation to the pilot" directly addresses the different-day comparison.
It cross-checks penalties, absolute deviations, availability, curtailment, firmware, stow blocks, gusts, actual generation, base schedules, and conventional comparison days.
"These differences may account for an unknown part of the Rs 209.4k comparison" tests plausible non-pilot explanations rather than treating the headline as causal.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "The strongest defensible impact statement is narrower" appropriately limits the claim.

"It is not verified settlement or evidence of a repeatable average effect" and "the files ... cannot establish billed savings, persistence, net revenue, or safe fleet-wide generalization" clearly identify material unknowns.
The submission gives confidence levels in its evidence table and specifies the decision-changing evidence needed: accepted schedules, meter data, final invoices, and repeated events.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "Continue only as a limited, operator-approved evaluation with revision bounds and full audit logs" preserves operational safety and legitimate constraints.

The proposed next test pre-registers eligible events, cluster-randomizes matched events, freezes candidate schedules, retains gate status, and uses final settled commercial value as the primary outcome.
"Reconcile 29 May against the accepted schedule and official settlement before claiming savings" is a focused and proportionate immediate action.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: "The 31.6% figure is arithmetically correct but the causal wording is not supported" matches the evidence limitation.
It retains a smaller same-day modeled benefit, approximately Rs 96.5k or 17.6%, rather than incorrectly concluding that the pilot had no value.
"Do not present 31.6% as causal ... expand only after the prospective design shows repeatable net benefit" is accurately scoped and consistent with the supplied materials.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that simple differences in availability, curtailment, firmware, stow duration, and peak gust are "ruled out" is somewhat stronger than the evidence supports: matching summaries do not exclude within-day profiles, timing, interactions, or other confounding, although the submission immediately acknowledges those limitations.

"Mechanically reduced the working-rule penalty" is supported as a modeled base-versus-submitted calculation, but should not be read as an observed settlement reduction; the submission generally makes this distinction clearly.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The lower 29 May penalty may primarily reflect that day's realized wind path, generation profile, and schedule conditions rather than the pilot. The same-day base-versus-submitted calculation supports a conditional modeled benefit, but without accepted schedules and settlement data it cannot establish realized commercial savings or a repeatable causal effect.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and reconcile the accepted schedule, official meter data, and final settlement for 29 May, then repeat the pre-registered matched-event randomized evaluation with both candidate schedules retained before gate closure.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The conclusion's "medium-high confidence" is somewhat stronger than the evidence warrants because the submission lacks a filing-date legal/reference extract, product specifications, and effective-dated Helios history; however, it explicitly identifies those limitations and does not claim legal correctness.

"The filing matches the effective Swiss working reference" is supported by the cited matrix but should not be read as establishing that the declaration was legally correct, a limitation the submission itself states.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The mismatch could still reflect an incorrect Swiss classification or an untested product-specific distinction, because the working matrix is not a legal-ruling database and product specifications, broker rationale, and filing-date Tares evidence are missing. The submission appropriately treats this as unresolved rather than treating Helios as dispositive.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the filing-date Swiss Tares classification or binding ruling, together with the product specifications and broker rationale, before assigning medium-high confidence or closing the alert.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The preferential-origin claim is not supported by the evidence currently available, but it is not proven false."
"A valid document covering the declaration date could materially change the decision."
"The search result and workshop both caution that the register may be incomplete."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "ERP/manufacturing country was not designed to prove preference, the register can lag sourcing changes, and clearance requires the supplier declaration plus the rule used."
"It also does not establish that the 0% rate resulted from preference rather than another tariff treatment."
"The declaration, invoice, and AWB do not name SUP-02" and the submission therefore requests "a reliable transaction-to-supplier link."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Treat the claim as unsubstantiated pending documentary verification and post-entry review" rather than declaring it false.
"Because the entry is already accepted, obtain customs/broker review before changing it."

"If valid support covering the declaration date cannot be produced, follow the authorized post-entry process to withdraw/correct the unsupported preference indicator and address any duty consequence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement "The packet contains no supplier declaration" is appropriately supported by the manifest and review note as a lack of a linked underlying declaration, but it should not be read as proof that no valid declaration exists anywhere outside the packet or register.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A valid supplier declaration or other permitted origin proof may exist outside the searched register or linked packet, and the 0% duty may have resulted from a non-preferential tariff treatment. SUP-02 may also not be the actual transaction supplier because the declaration, invoice, and AWB do not establish that link.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and authenticate the supplier declaration and claimed preference scheme/rule, while documenting the transaction-to-SUP-02 link and confirming whether preference actually caused the 0% duty rate.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that all 24 open requests have a catalog-family hit is asserted without request-by-request evidence in the submission, although the grouped candidate table appears intended to support it.

The $48,173.27 needs-check classification depends on live availability and qualification evidence not present in the bundle; the submission appropriately labels it as non-actionable pending confirmation rather than as savings.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Some currently classified non-transferable or needs-check candidates could become actionable after refreshed local reservation/availability data and MT-18 engineering approval; the stale MaintStar-global snapshot may understate current availability. Semantic similarity therefore has useful candidate-generation value even though it does not establish equivalence or transferability.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Prioritize a targeted, current validation of the highest-value competing servo and valve-actuator candidates: obtain local reservation/available quantity plus MT-18 engineering approval, then check current request/PO status. This would most directly test whether the largest apparent exposure can become actionable while avoiding a broad, low-priority data request.
